rationale: OWNER RULING 2026-08-21, closing RFC_041 §5's open question: 'make it just one spelling and create a check for that. do it while it's cheap.' THE DEFECT SHAPE. Until today this package offered two ways to render a component: RenderTemplateReportingMissing, which returns the empty-placeholder report and the dead-URL-attribute report, and a one-line RenderTemplate wrapper that threw both away. Nine of the twelve non-test call sites used the short one — which is exactly how bugs_open/238 shipped five to a live homepage while the call had the field names in hand. The discard was INSIDE the wrapper, where no reviewer of the call site could see it. dead_url_guard.go's own header says so: 'RenderTemplate throws it away (out, _, _ :=), and RenderComponentAction calls RenderTemplate. The finding has been available, by name, on the failing path, for the whole life of the defect.' THE FIX. One spelling: RenderTemplate now IS the reporting form, (string, []string, []string, error), and the wrapper is deleted. A caller that does not want the reports writes `out, _, _, err :=`, so the discard is in the diff where a reviewer of the CALL SITE sees it. 16 call sites updated across 11 files including cmd/component-render-check and another lane's tool_birth_instance_scope.go (committed this morning, clean in the tree — not a passenger). WHY NOW AND NOT IN THE 238 LANE, which named this move and declined it: that round's reason was 'making RenderTemplate itself the reporting form fleet-wide changes the primitive every render flows through — the RFC-shaped move, not a rider on a bug fix.' It became cheap once bugs_closed/260 gave every caller an error to handle, because the diff is then mechanical rather than behavioural: every site already had a multi-value assignment. There is NO behaviour change in this submission's first half — same function body, same reports, same error, one name. THE CHECK, which is the half the owner asked for and the half that found something. Three AST-based tests (render_seam_one_spelling_test.go). (1) TestOnlyOneExportedRenderTemplateSpelling: the set of exported RenderTemplate* symbols must be exactly {RenderTemplate, RenderTemplateWithMap}. (2) TestOneEntryPointToTheExecutor: the set of functions calling executeGoTemplate must be exactly {RenderTemplate} — a second entry point would skip the form_action seeding, the InstanceID report, missingBareFields, the strip and the error channel, all of which live in the seam AROUND the execution. (3) TestTemplateExecutorsAreDeclared: the set of functions that CONSTRUCT AND EXECUTE a Go template must equal a declared, grouped allow-list. AST AND NOT GREP, deliberately: a source-scanning check makes your COMMENTS load-bearing, and this file's own prose names the deleted symbol to explain the history — a grep rule would fail on itself. Proven by mutation: re-adding a convenience wrapper fails (1); a stale allow-list entry fails (3) in the OTHER direction, because the sets are compared exactly so a list that only grows cannot stop discriminating; a control asserts the traversal parsed >=100 functions, so a broken parse cannot pass everything for the wrong reason. WHAT THE CHECK FOUND ON ITS FIRST RUN, and this is the part worth a reviewer's attention: SEVEN more functions in this package execute Go templates, none of them enumerated anywhere. Five are unrelated (commit message, storage path, search query, workflow condition, CSS-from-spec) and are declared as such. The sixth, missingBareFields, only PARSES — which is why rule (3) requires construct AND execute rather than construct alone, or the list would fill with parse-only helpers nobody needs to justify. THE SEVENTH IS A THIRD COMPONENT-HTML EXECUTOR WITH ITS OWN DIALECT AND ITS OWN SILENT FALLBACK: renderBlogTemplate (rebuild_blog_listing_action.go) executes a component's html_template with template.New(...).Parse and NO FuncMap and NO missingkey=zero — the same divergence as RenderTemplateWithMap (bugs_closed/260 §13g), except that this path is LIVE: rebuild_blog_listing is a registered action, where §13g's chain ends at an unregistered one. And on a PARSE failure it logged at Warn and silently rendered defaultBlogListingTemplate instead — so a site whose listing template could not be parsed shipped a GENERIC listing, its own design silently replaced, with nothing downstream able to tell. That is bugs_closed/260's defect in a second place and it is fixed in this submission: parse and execute failures both return an error, and the caller already failed the step on empty output, so the two failure modes finally agree. MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING IT [2026-08-21]: exactly ONE live blog-listing component (blog-listing_pre_037, 6,413 bytes) and it uses NONE of the missing FuncMap names — so no live template can trip the parse error today. This closes the door before someone edits one, not after. STATED RISK, because it is the honest one: this converts a silent substitution into a step failure on a live path, and a failed step on this estate currently has a separate problem — see risks. SCOPE AND REGISTRATION: no new capability, no new config key, no DB change, no migration. RFC_041 §5 is answered rather than extended, and the concept-register entry STY-057 gains the one-spelling rule and the third executor.

plan.summary: Collapse two render spellings into one and make it structural. RenderTemplate becomes the reporting form (string, []string, []string, error); the one-line wrapper that discarded both reports is deleted; 16 call sites across 11 files are updated so every discard is written at the call site as `_, _`. Three AST guard tests then hold the property: one exported RenderTemplate* set, one caller of executeGoTemplate, and an exact-match declared list of template EXECUTORS (construct AND execute, so parse-only helpers stay out). The third test found seven undeclared executors on its first run, one of which — renderBlogTemplate — is a third component-HTML executor on a LIVE registered path with no FuncMap and a silent substitution of a generic default listing on parse failure; that substitution is removed here, measured safe against the one live blog-listing component. No behaviour change anywhere else: same body, same reports, same error, one name.

edits.rationale: The rename plus the deletion IS the change. Keeping the short name for the reporting form (rather than keeping the long name) is deliberate: the natural name should be the safe one, so the path of least resistance stops being the lossy path.

Its header is the clearest existing statement of WHY the two spellings were a defect, written in the present tense about a state that no longer exists. Left alone it would tell the next reader the wrapper is still there.

plan.risks: 1) ⚠ THE ONE REAL RISK, and it is not in this diff: renderBlogTemplate's parse failure now FAILS THE STEP where it used to ship a generic listing — and a failed step on this estate is currently swallowed. Measured today while investigating an unrelated diagnosis item: 192 work items in the six days BEFORE 2026-08-20 were stamped `complete` while carrying a step failure in their own `error` column (22 of them via validate_content), and 11 since. So a blog-listing parse failure would fail the step, park nothing, and stamp the item complete. That defect is pre-existing and general (it is NOT introduced by this change or by bugs_closed/260 — the split at the roll proves it), it has a filed needs_diagnosis item whose run failed, and it is the reason a reviewer should NOT read 'fails the step' as 'is visible'. Mitigated here only by measurement: no live blog template can trip the parse branch. 2) The signature change touches 11 files including two other lanes' (tool_birth_instance_scope.go, and the audit binary), and HEAD is shared — half a signature change is what broke HEAD on 2026-08-20. Mitigated by committing narrowly and immediately and by a worktree build at HEAD after committing. 3) Eight `_, _` discards are now visible; a reviewer may reasonably ask why each site ignores the dead-control report. That is the intended consequence and the honest answer is that nobody has decided for those paths yet — the discards are a to-do list, not a design. 4) The declared-executor list is a new allow-list, i.e. a new thing that can rot; mitigated by the exact-match rule, which fails on a stale entry as loudly as on a missing one. 5) No DB change, no config key, no migration, and nothing here is gated — so there is nothing to arm and nothing to roll back beyond the code.
